# 1010Benja shows Suno can be more than an AI music slop engine (The Verge)

By Terrence O'Brien. Published July 19, 2026.

## Key findings
- **1010Benja** is unapologetic about using generative AI on his latest EP, **"Time Has Nothing To Do With What You Choose…"** (the opener being **"Semiramis' Dream"**).
- The EP is the follow-up to 2024's **"Ten Total"** (which earned a Pitchfork Best New Music tag).
- Process: Benja and friend **Patrick Holder** did the beat; Benja recorded the vocals; then they **fed Suno the elements**, settled on something, **edited it on Ableton**, and **put it back into Suno** — repeated a few hundred times.
- Benja: "So when you look in Deezer, it marks the song as AI-generated. We're not hiding it. We don't feel any shame about it."
- Benja wrote the lyrics and sang the vocals; the AI (a Suno-generated children's choir) is layered in. He frames using gen-AI as economic: "The only reason I'm using gen at all is because my visions are currently far beyond my means."
- O'Brien (a longtime Suno skeptic) concluded: "1010Benja hasn't converted me... But he has proven that, in the right hands, Suno doesn't have to be a slop engine."

## Assessment
- `authoritative: yes` — The Verge is a top-tier outlet.
- Establishes: 1010Benja (human rapper/artist) actively uses Suno in his released music (EP "Time Has Nothing To Do With What You Choose…", 2026; track "Semiramis' Dream"), with human vocals/lyrics layered through a repeated Suno/Ableton loop, and does not hide the AI credit (Deezer flags it AI-generated).
